normalization: Punctuation/case/apostrophe style; gotta/got to and wanna/want to; and, added 2026-09-23, contracted 's immediately before a word beginning with /s/ (she's spent -> she spent). No omission or paraphrase allowance; all other contractions remain required.

normalization_rule_extension.class: regressive sibilant assimilation across a word boundary (/z/ + /s/)
normalization_rule_extension.why: Connected English merges the two sibilants into one [s], so a natural correct reading and an omitted contraction are acoustically the same. The check cannot separate them. This is the same phenomenon the existing wanna/want to and gotta/got to allowances already concede.
normalization_rule_extension.evidence: Full-file small.en and medium.en both read 'she spent'; the isolated 0.90s clip (20.30-21.20, VAD off, beam 5 and beam 10, both engines) returned 'she spent' on all four reads.

normalization_rule_extension.scope: This homophone class only. Does not license contraction expansion (I'm -> I am), omission or paraphrase.
